When Archivist and Archmage Aziraphale Fell accepts a new position from the Crown, he expects difficult work; maintaining ancient seals and preserving private records of their intense magic has never had a reputation for being easy, after all.
Instead, he finds unanswered questions he is forbade from asking, and a peculiar sort of loneliness waiting amongst dusty records, weary magic, and cold cobblestone.
What really catches him off guard, however, is not the work itself, but rather discovering something worth asking forbidden questions for—something that leaves him counting the hours until he can return, whilst trying not to wonder whether that something has begun counting with him.

title: The Oldest Trick in London Below

summary:
When an immortal swordsman falls through the cracks of the world, he lands in a city that shouldn’t exist — and in the path of one very charming, very impossible man.
Methos, oldest of the Immortals, wakes in London Below after a quickening gone wrong. There are talking rats, murderous velvet assassins, and a man in a tattered coat who introduces himself as the Marquis de Carabas: thief, liar, and occasional savior of fools.
Together, they barter in memories, con minor gods, and argue over whose bad habits are worse. Somewhere between haunted umbrellas, near-death escapes, and too much banter under too little light, they begin to see something familiar in each other — the same exhaustion, the same hunger to keep living no matter the cost.
And when dawn finally touches the Thames, the oldest liar in history finds himself believing in one more trick: love.

title: Button Eyes

summary: Y/N signed the last closing document with a joyous tremor, the keys to her very first home, the notorious Pink Palace, feeling heavy and glorious in her palm. The tiny, crooked Victorian, painted an aggressive coral, felt like the perfect symbol of her fresh start. Little did she know the charming young man who sold it to her, Wybee, was doing the darkness a favor. He had knowingly delivered her into the clutches of the ancient horror supposedly trapped behind the miniature, almost invisible door in the basement—a dread he had hoped died forty years prior. But the Oathbreaker hadn't perished; it had merely shifted its appetite. No longer focused on stealing children, the oathbreaker who saw himself as a connoisseur now "cherished" beautiful women, meticulously peeling away their youth and eating their souls like candied fruit. As Y/N stepped over the threshold, a pair of glistening, obsidian button eyes watched from the deepest shadows of the house—and in that chilling, inhuman gaze, she was utterly, devastatingly perfect.

Between sword fights, stolen wine, and jokes about divine metabolism, they find what neither expected: companionship that refuses to die.

title: The Gentleman’s Bargain
author: brmqtr
summary:
London Below runs on bargains — dark, glittering, and never fair.
Richard Mayhew, still half a stranger to its dangers, wants only to survive. The Marquis de Carabas, equal parts charm and trickery, offers to teach him the rules. In exchange, Richard must teach the Marquis something far more impossible: how to be decent.
Their lessons spiral through markets of mirrors, poisoned tea, and too many near-deaths. Richard learns cunning; the Marquis learns courtesy (begrudgingly). Between the arguments and rescues, humor sharpens into affection, and decency becomes the most dangerous thing either of them has ever tried.
The Gentleman’s Bargain is a sharp, seductive reimagining of Neil Gaiman’s Neverwhere — a story of wit, danger, and reluctant tenderness, where a dead rat can open doors, and two men discover that survival and sincerity might just mean the same thing.

title: Tea, Blood, and Other Negotiations
author: brmqtr
summary:
Richard Mayhew thought life in London Above would go back to normal. A job, a flat, perhaps even a quiet evening without someone threatening him with a crossbow. Instead, he finds a bloodstained coat, a dying man on his carpet, and the familiar voice of the Marquis de Carabas saying, “Don’t ruin my evening—or my outfit.”
What begins as one more favor owed quickly turns into a journey back through the cracks of London Below, where mirrors whisper, debts breathe, and friendship is more dangerous than magic. Between assassins, talking rats, and an ill-advised sandwich incident, Richard learns that the Marquis’s talent for chaos might only be matched by his knack for coming back.
A story about doors, impossible men, and the fine art of surviving love—one bargain at a time.

title: Danger Is the Fun Part
author: brmqtr
summary:
When the Marquis de Carabas — trickster, survivor, and master of wit — finds himself stranded in the Grand Line, he expects to charm or cheat his way back to safety. Instead, he’s hauled aboard the Thousand Sunny and thrown into the orbit of Monkey D. Luffy, a captain with rubber fists, a boundless grin, and absolutely no regard for caution.
Where the Marquis schemes with words and shadows, Luffy charges headfirst with laughter and fists. Together they face shadowy islands, pirate ambushes, and storms that could tear the sea apart. To the Marquis’s surprise, they make a terrifyingly effective team. To his greater surprise, he finds himself caught off guard by Luffy’s simple honesty — and by the way a blunt “I like you” can shake him more than any knife.
It’s a story of tricks and tides, danger and laughter, and the most perilous adventure of all: falling in love with a Straw Hat.
